0.original: Seigetsu the Enlightened hopes to enlist the aid of ancient Namazu spirits.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Please note that the difficulty of this quest has been synced to your current level. Furthermore, you may not proceed with a class or job that is different from when you accepted this quest.

2.original: You have spoken with the Namazu steward.<hex:02100103>Deliver the requested supplies to Seigetsu the Enlightened.

48.original: <hex:021A020203>The Chrysanthemum and the Dango<hex:021A020103> describes a Hingan ritual in which the spirits of their ancestors are beckoned into the home to ensure a bountiful harvest.

49.original: We will perform these selfsame rites here in Dhoro Iloh. Should the souls of our forebears answer the call, their divine protection may prove instrumental in averting our impending doom.

50.original: One of the Seven Hundred Seventy-Seven is searching the plains for the necessary offerings. As this was not originally a custom of the Namazu, there may be matters best handled by someone with...hands. Think of it as another opportunity to prove your usefulness!

51.original: Did Gyofun...I mean, Seigetsu the Enlightened send you? I'm so inundated with tasks, I can't possibly manage them alone. I need your help!

52.original: We need traditional serving trays to present the food for the kami! Please, look inside that crate and see if there's anything you can use!

53.original: We need a traditional serving mat to present the offerings! Please, look inside that crate and see if there's anything you can use!

54.original: We need traditional delicacies to present as offerings! Please, look inside that crate and see if there's anything you can use!

55.original: I was told to gather steppe clay for making traditional Hingan crockery. You'll go and get some for me, won't you? Try searching a little south of Chakha Zoh. Yes, yes.

56.original: I was told to gather ingredients for traditional Hingan dishes, but I can't find any edible buds! I heard they grow south of Chakha Zoh, but I couldn't find any for the life of me. Perhaps you will have better luck. Yes, yes.

57.original: We need a steppe sweetfish, the centerpiece of the offerings! Could you catch one from Tao Khaal? Apparently, they are drawn to the smell of salmon roe. Yes, yes.

58.original: When you're done, please go straight to Seigetsu. He is insistent that he is the only one capable of arranging the offerings as tradition dictates. Yes, yes.

59.original: Did you have a mishap? Not to worry, there are more materials in the crate.

60.original: Did you have a mishap? Not to worry, there are more materials in the crate.

61.original: So the delicacy didn't turn out as well as you'd hoped? Not to worry, there are more ingredients in the crate.

62.original: The crate appears to be filled to the brim with sundry materials─none of which you require at this time.

69.original: You can't find any steppe clay? Try looking south of Chakha Zoh.

70.original: You can't find any edible buds? Try looking south of Chakha Zoh.

71.original: Are the steppe sweetfish eluding you? There should be plenty in Tao Khaal. Yes, yes.

72.original: You've done ever so well! I'm sure Seigetsu will approve. Yes, yes.

73.original: Do you have something to present to me?

74.original: Let me see... Yes, yes, perfectly adequate. Once the offerings have been suitably blessed and arranged, all that will remain is to perform the ritual itself.

75.original: Part of the ceremony involves enacting a banquet as though our long-dead ancestors are corporeally present. The process is extremely lengthy and involves chanting in an ancient Hingan tongue.

76.original: I dare not entrust such a delicate task to any of my Namazu brethren, who would no doubt botch the incantations and leave us all cursed to eternal damnation.
